competencies.description: Data Processing is the ability to acquire, clean, transform, combine, and document data so it is fit for analysis and reporting. In this context, it includes connecting to multiple data sources, resolving quality issues, shaping data structures, and preparing datasets for semantic models and downstream analytics in Power BI.
indicators: Combine multiple datasets from different sources using joins or merges based on common keys, handling inconsistencies in data structure.
Write scripts to automate common data cleaning tasks, such as removing duplicates, correcting data types, and normalizing values.
Perform complex data manipulations and transformations (e.g., data aggregation, time series processing).
Review and analyze outliers and their role as a potential root cause for quality issues.
Provide transparent documentation and rationale for dataset fitness for use.

competencies.description: Technical Communication is the ability to translate analytical findings into clear, structured, and audience-appropriate narratives and visual products. For this course, it includes designing reports and dashboards, selecting effective visuals, supporting storytelling, and communicating insights in ways that are understandable and useful for business stakeholders.
indicators: Organize data insights into a clear, logical structure, ensuring the narrative flow is easy to follow and the key insights are highlighted.
Create complex visualizations (e.g., heatmaps, scatter plots, time series plots) to demonstrate trends, correlations, or distributions, providing more detailed insights for specific audiences.
Adapt communication approach for different stakeholders (e.g., technical team vs. business Leaders), ensuring that the level of complexity is appropriate for the audience.
Develop data-driven narratives that directly link findings to business objectives, demonstrating how the insights impact strategy and decision-making.
Communicate risks of AI-generated content (e.g., copyright, bias, etc.).

competencies.competency: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
competencies.description: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect is the ability to apply ethical, legal, privacy, security, and accessibility standards in the use of data and analytics tools. In this study guide, this is reflected through managing access, configuring row-level security, applying sensitivity labels, setting privacy levels, and designing accessible reports that support responsible use of analytics and AI-enabled features.
indicators: Apply legal and ethical standards when using data, methods, and resources.
Use principles for responsible use of AI in government.
Assess source data for bias, representation, validity and accuracy.
Ensure all visuals meet accessibility/digital standards.

title: Pro Git (Official Book)
description: This comprehensive official book develops practical proficiency in Git as a distributed version control system. Learners build skills in repository setup, change tracking, branching and merging, remote collaboration, workflow management, server configuration, troubleshooting, and advanced Git internals to support collaborative software and data project delivery.

competencies.description: Code Management is the ability to use version control practices to organize, document, and maintain code changes in a collaborative environment. It includes understanding the purpose of version control systems, applying basic repository workflows, and supporting consistent project structure and traceability.
indicators: Recall the purpose of version control systems (e.g., Git) and their role in collaborative coding.
Explain the need for basic code documentation and consistent file structures in projects that involve programming.
Execute basic version control commands (e.g., git commit, git push) to manage code changes.

competencies.competency: Working Effectively with Others (Mobilize People; Collaborate with Partners and Stakeholders)
competencies.description: Working Effectively with Others is the ability to collaborate productively with team members and contributors to achieve shared outcomes. In this context, it includes participating in distributed workflows, sharing changes through remotes and hosted platforms, and contributing to projects in ways that support coordinated teamwork.
indicators: Share relevant information to facilitate collaboration.
Accomplish independent tasks as part of one's own share of the work.
Work with others to clearly define problems and identify suitable solutions.
Openly share data/findings to support other teams' work.

competencies.description: Project Management is the ability to support organized delivery by following structured workflows, maintaining records, and helping keep work on track. Through Git-based practices such as branching, tagging, history inspection, and workflow discipline, learners strengthen their ability to contribute to controlled and traceable project execution.
indicators: Understand and follow project timelines and task lists.
Contribute to maintaining project documentation (e.g., status reports, project timelines) and keep records updated.

title: GitLab Official Tutorials
description: This learning resource provides guided tutorials on core GitLab capabilities, including Git-based version control, repository and workflow management, project planning, CI/CD pipelines, security and compliance scanning, deployment, infrastructure management, integrations, and AI-assisted development features.

competencies.description: Code Management is the ability to use version control practices and basic documentation approaches to organize, track, and collaborate on code changes effectively within development projects.
indicators: Recall the purpose of version control systems (e.g., Git) and their role in collaborative coding.
Explain the need for basic code documentation and consistent file structures in projects that involve programming.
Execute basic version control commands (e.g., git commit, git push) to manage code changes.

competencies.description: Project Management is the ability to organize, monitor, and support the delivery of work by managing tasks, timelines, risks, stakeholder communication, and feedback throughout the project lifecycle.
indicators: Independently manage smaller, less complex tasks within a project, ensuring deadlines and deliverables are met.
Provide regular updates to stakeholders on the status of the project, ensuring clear communication of timelines, issues, and changes.
Engage with users to collect feedback/data during idea/solution implementation.
Flag AI/data governance issues.
Register new AI solutions/projects with appropriate stakeholders.

competencies.competency: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
competencies.description: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect is the ability to apply legal, ethical, privacy, security, and accessibility standards responsibly when using digital tools, data, and AI-enabled capabilities in the workplace.
indicators: Apply legal and ethical standards when using data, methods, and resources.
Use principles for responsible use of AI in government.
Ensure all visuals meet accessibility/digital standards.

title: Learn Git Branching
description: This interactive course develops practical proficiency with Git version control through guided, visual exercises. Learners practice core and advanced concepts such as commits, branching, merging, rebasing, detached HEAD states, remote workflows, and command-line operations in a sandbox environment.

competencies.description: Code Management is the ability to use version control practices to organize, document, and manage code changes in collaborative development environments. It includes understanding the purpose of version control systems and applying basic commands to track and maintain code effectively.
indicators: Recall the purpose of version control systems (e.g., Git) and their role in collaborative coding.
Explain the need for basic code documentation and consistent file structures in projects that involve programming.
Execute basic version control commands (e.g., git commit, git push) to manage code changes.

competencies.description: Programming is the ability to use coding tools and command-based workflows to perform technical tasks in a structured and reliable way. In this context, it includes applying basic command-line practices and working with open-source tools to support software development activities.
indicators: Consider use of open source over commercial tools.

title: W3Schools SQL Tutorial
description: This beginner-level tutorial introduces SQL as a standard language for storing, retrieving, and manipulating data in relational databases. Through interactive examples, exercises, quizzes, and reference materials, learners build foundational skills in writing queries, filtering results, joining tables, understanding data types, and performing common database operations across major database platforms.

competencies.description: Data Processing at the foundational level involves loading, preparing, transforming, and organizing data so it can be used effectively for analysis and operational tasks. It includes applying basic data handling techniques and understanding how data moves through its lifecycle.
indicators: Load datasets from common formats (CSV, Excel, SQL) and perform basic cleaning tasks such as handling missing values and formatting issues.
Apply data transformations such as filtering, aggregating, and sorting to prepare data for analysis.
Derive variables to enhance data analysis.
Describe the stages of the full data lifecycle (plan, collect, process, use, share, dispose).

competencies.description: Technical Communication at the foundational level involves using appropriate technical terminology and clearly explaining basic data concepts, outputs, and results so they are understandable to learners and stakeholders.
indicators: Use appropriate data/AI terms and concepts when communicating.

competencies.competency: Thinking Things Through (Create Vision and Strategy)
competencies.description: Thinking Things Through at the foundational level involves approaching problems logically, identifying relevant questions, and using structured reasoning to interpret information and support practical solutions.
indicators: Ask the right questions to identify relevant problems/issues.
Use cause and effect relationships to analyze problems systematically.
Resolve problems in a sound, logical and decisive manner.

title: Microsoft Learn SQL Server Resources
description: This learning collection provides foundational to intermediate instruction on SQL Server and Azure SQL administration and querying. It covers connecting and querying with SSMS, writing Transact-SQL, backup and restore, monitoring, replication, high availability, database security, performance tuning, and selecting appropriate deployment models across on-premises and Azure environments.

competencies.description: Data Processing is the ability to load, prepare, transform, and manage data so it can be used reliably for analysis and operational purposes. At the foundational level, it includes working with common data sources, applying basic transformations, and understanding the stages of the data lifecycle.
indicators: Load datasets from common formats (CSV, Excel, SQL) and perform basic cleaning tasks such as handling missing values and formatting issues.
Apply data transformations such as filtering, aggregating, and sorting to prepare data for analysis.
Describe the stages of the full data lifecycle (plan, collect, process, use, share, dispose).

competencies.description: Business Acumen is the ability to understand organizational needs and align technical choices with operational objectives. In this context, it includes selecting suitable SQL platform options, understanding how database solutions support business and service requirements, and relating technical decisions to intended operational use.
indicators: Collaborate with business teams to identify key business objectives and tailor data science projects to align with those objectives.
Assess the potential impact of data science solutions on business performance and communicate how the findings can influence business decisions.
Work with cross-functional teams (e.g., marketing, finance, product) to ensure data projects are aligned with business priorities.

competencies.competency: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect (Upholds Integrity and Respect)
competencies.description: Demonstrating Integrity and Respect is the ability to apply legal, ethical, privacy, and security requirements in day-to-day technical work. For SQL Server and Azure SQL environments, this includes recognizing privacy and security implications, following organizational frameworks, and consulting appropriate guidance when handling protected data and access controls.
indicators: Adhere to the organization's legal, privacy and ethical frameworks (Privacy Act, Policy on Privacy Protection, etc.) and follow disclosure procedures.
Identify and proactively flag privacy/security/accessibility implications.
Ensure privacy/security is set at the right permission levels.

title: Oracle Dev Gym SQL Course
description: This interactive course introduces core Oracle SQL concepts and relational database fundamentals. Learners practice writing queries, filtering and retrieving data, combining tables with joins, understanding transactions, and applying foundational data modeling concepts in an Oracle environment.

competencies.description: Data Processing is the ability to load, clean, transform, and prepare data for analysis or operational use. At the foundational level, it includes working with common data sources and applying basic transformations to make data usable and meaningful.
indicators: Load datasets from common formats (CSV, Excel, SQL) and perform basic cleaning tasks such as handling missing values and formatting issues.
Apply data transformations such as filtering, aggregating, and sorting to prepare data for analysis.
Derive variables to enhance data analysis.

competencies.description: Technical Communication is the ability to express data and technical concepts clearly and appropriately for the intended audience. At the foundational level, it involves using correct terminology and presenting information in a straightforward and understandable way.
indicators: Use appropriate data/AI terms and concepts when communicating.

competencies.description: Business Acumen is the ability to understand how data-related work supports organizational operations and decision-making. At the foundational level, it includes recognizing the value of data as an organizational asset and understanding how data work connects to business needs.
indicators: Recognize various data types and value as an organizational asset.

title: Microsoft OneLake Documentation
description: This documentation introduces Microsoft OneLake as the unified logical data lake within Microsoft Fabric. It explains core architecture, storage concepts, shortcuts, Azure integration, deployment considerations, and basic setup steps for enabling organization-wide data access without managing underlying infrastructure.

competencies.description: Data Processing is the ability to understand how data is loaded, transformed, organized, and managed across its lifecycle so it can be used effectively for analysis and operations. At the foundational level, it includes understanding common data formats, basic preparation steps, and the stages involved in storing, using, sharing, and maintaining data.
indicators: Describe the stages of the full data lifecycle (plan, collect, process, use, share, dispose).

competencies.description: Business Acumen is the ability to understand how technology and data assets support organizational objectives and operational needs. At the foundational level, it includes recognizing the value of data as an organizational asset and understanding how data platforms can support business and program outcomes.
indicators: Recognize various data types and value as an organizational asset.

competencies.competency: Thinking Things Through (Create Vision and Strategy)
competencies.description: Thinking Things Through is the ability to understand problems, identify relevant relationships, and form practical recommendations based on available information. At the foundational level, it includes recognizing connections between systems, concepts, and operational needs in order to support sound planning and implementation decisions.
indicators: Recognize connections and develop short-term plans and recommendations.

title: Microsoft Fabric Learning Labs
description: This hands-on lab introduces learners to discovering, accessing, and analyzing organizational data in Microsoft Fabric OneLake. Participants create a workspace and lakehouse, ingest CSV data into a Delta table, inspect metadata and schema through the OneLake catalog, create cross-workspace shortcuts, query data with SQL, and build a semantic model for exploratory analytics.

competencies.description: Data Processing is the ability to prepare, transform, organize, and document data so it can be reliably used for analysis and reporting. This includes working with multiple data formats, performing structured transformations, and maintaining transparency about how datasets are prepared and used.
indicators: Process both structured data (e.g., databases, spreadsheets) and unstructured data (e.g., text, logs) for analysis.
Perform complex data manipulations and transformations (e.g., data aggregation, time series processing).
Provide transparent documentation and rationale for dataset fitness for use.

competencies.description: Technical Communication is the ability to organize and present data insights in a clear, logical, and audience-appropriate way. It includes structuring findings, adapting explanations for different stakeholders, and linking analytical outputs to decision-making needs.
indicators: Organize data insights into a clear, logical structure, ensuring the narrative flow is easy to follow and the key insights are highlighted.
Adapt communication approach for different stakeholders (e.g., technical team vs. business Leaders), ensuring that the level of complexity is appropriate for the audience.
Develop data-driven narratives that directly link findings to business objectives, demonstrating how the insights impact strategy and decision-making.

competencies.description: Business Acumen is the ability to connect data activities to organizational objectives and operational needs. It involves understanding how data assets, analytics workflows, and reporting tools support decision-making and business value across teams.
indicators: Collaborate with business teams to identify key business objectives and tailor data science projects to align with those objectives.
Work with cross-functional teams (e.g., marketing, finance, product) to ensure data projects are aligned with business priorities.
Tie visualizations explicitly to business rationale and intended use.
